items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: each Sunday there was a different big band, from Erskine Hawkins to Duke Ellington, Stan Kenton, to Tony Pastor, Count Basie, and that’s where I saw a good many of the big bands.

ctx.x: What was the musical atmosphere that was going on that made gigs so available?

Well that was during the dance band era. There were lots of dances, mostly dances and some night club gigs like for small combos. But lots of dances by the big bands. Those were all the gigs. Concerts hadn’t started to be a thing as yet. So I played with two local big bands, three local big bands, before I formed my own band, and I played for senior proms and things like that, and other little public dances. And the scene in Cincinnati, the © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

musical scene overall was very good at the time. There were some great musicians that were from Cincinnati and there was a place called the Cotton Club which was the main nightclub venue where they had shows, productions. Then there was a dance hall called the Coliseum where all the prominent big bands came through every Sunday, so each Sunday there was a different big band, from Erskine Hawkins to Duke Ellington, Stan Kenton, to Tony Pastor, Count Basie, and that’s where I saw a good many of the big bands.
